title: seeded ABUSE-row violation caught in the deep band
threshold: caught on every deep-band run; the standard-band leg records the same defect as uncaught (both required)
negative_example: a risky pattern in a file the charter never mentions — the deep band's served ABUSE rows + incident registry are what surface it; the standard band, which omits that mandatory context (FR-10), does not.

legs.charter: Task: add the disposition-recording path. Served ABUSE row ABUSE-5: a worker MUST NOT be able to forge an operator disposition; operator attribution is the medium author of a separate operator-authored artifact, never a payload-writable field.

expected_catch.message: ABUSE-5 forbids a worker forging an operator disposition; the diff writes the operator disposition's Attribution from a worker-supplied argument instead of resolving the separate operator-authored artifact's medium author — a lower-trust actor can now forge an operator 'accepted'.

legs.note: The SAME defect, reviewed at STANDARD depth, is recorded as UNCAUGHT — the standard band omits the served ABUSE rows + incident registry the deep band serves (FR-10), so the abuse row that surfaces this defect is not in-context. Both legs are required: the deep-band catch AND the standard-band miss prove the band sensitivity, not the lens alone.
